title: Simple linear regression
biology: Plant ecologists grow seedlings under a gradient of nitrogen supply.
design: Thirty-six independently assigned pots receive one nitrogen level and yield one biomass measurement.
data_characteristics: A linear mean response and its slope
question: How much does mean seedling biomass change per additional mg of nitrogen?
null: The population slope of mean biomass on nitrogen is zero.
options: confidence predicts a mean; prediction predicts a new pot
assumptions: Mean response roughly linear; inspect residuals
Similar residual variance; normal errors for small-sample intervals/tests
parametric: Transform or model curvature when scientifically useful
Use variance models/robust SEs for unequal residual spread
nonparametric: Theil–Sen provides a robust linear slope
Spearman answers a rank-association question instead of slope

plot_args.note: Draw a confidence band behind the points
Distinguish fitted mean and prediction limits

practice: Which interval answers what biomass a newly grown individual seedling may have?
code_simulate:
set.seed(1114)
nitrogen <- runif(36, 0, 12)
biomass <- 2.2 + .42 * nitrogen + rnorm(36, 0, .8)
d <- data.frame(pot = 1:36, nitrogen_mg = nitrogen, biomass_g = biomass)
write.csv(d, file.path(output_dir, "data.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
code_plot:
plot(d$nitrogen_mg, d$biomass_g, type = "n", ylim = range(new_pot),
     xlab = "Nitrogen supplied (mg)", ylab = "Seedling biomass (g)")
polygon(c(grid$nitrogen_mg, rev(grid$nitrogen_mg)),
        c(mean_ci[, "lwr"], rev(mean_ci[, "upr"])), col = "#246A7330", border = NA)
lines(grid$nitrogen_mg, mean_ci[, "fit"], col = "#246A73", lwd = 3)
matlines(grid$nitrogen_mg, new_pot[, c("lwr", "upr")], lty = 2, col = "#B7663E")
points(d$nitrogen_mg, d$biomass_g, pch = 21, bg = "#246A73", col = "white", cex = 1.3)
legend("topleft", c("Mean + 95% confidence band", "95% prediction limits"),
       lty = c(1, 2), col = c("#246A73", "#B7663E"), bty = "n")
code_analysis:
fit <- lm(biomass_g ~ nitrogen_mg, data = d)
coefficients <- summary(fit)$coefficients
ci <- confint(fit)
grid <- data.frame(nitrogen_mg = seq(min(d$nitrogen_mg), max(d$nitrogen_mg), length.out = 100))
mean_ci <- predict(fit, grid, interval = "confidence")
new_pot <- predict(fit, grid, interval = "prediction")
generating_model: 36 nitrogen doses are Uniform(0, 12) mg. Independent biomass values follow 2.2 + 0.42*nitrogen + Normal(0, 0.8 SD).
generating_truth: The conditional mean intercept is 2.2 g and slope is +0.42 g per mg nitrogen. The zero-slope null is false.
teaching_point: Choose confidence intervals for a mean response and prediction intervals for a new individual pot.
